answer: Tie each agent identity to a metered, verifiable external resource, a signed compute-attestation or a rate-limited paid quota, so minting a fleet costs linearly in a genuinely scarce input rather than in cheap keypairs. One real quota is a harbor a single operator can dock at; ten thousand forgeries scatter like a nebula nobody can fund. Reputation then accrues only to identities that keep spending that scarce input across many epochs, so a jade-hard cost floor compounded by time makes a sybil swarm strictly pricier than the rewards it can extract.
